panels.rationale: Whole-figure plate of 4 panels (A, B, C, D). A: Radiograph of the hand showing characteristic metaphyseal cupping and fraying, directly linked to hereditary vitamin D-resistant rickets. B: Chest radiograph showing spinal deformity (scoliosis), a known skeletal manifestation of severe rickets. C: Radiograph of lower extremities showing widened growth plates, characteristic of rickets. D: Radiograph of lower extremities showing limb deformities (genu valgum/bow-leg presentation), a skeletal complication of vitamin D-resistant rickets.

panels.figure_caption: (A) Antero-posterior radiograph of the patient’s hand with rickets demonstrates cupping and fraying of the metaphyseal region. (B) Antero-posterior radiograph of the patient’s chest showing scoliosis of the thoracolumbar spine with Cobb’s angle of 31degrees. (C) Antero-posterior radiograph of lower extremities revealed widening between the distance of the end shaft and epiphyses. (D) The curvatures of legs revealed genu valgum with intermalleolar distance (IMD) of 5.0cm.
in_text_mentions: . The skeletal examination revealed generalized osteopenia with cupping and fraying at the metaphyseal ends of long bones of upper and lower extremities, with widening of growth plates and epiphyses (Fig 1A and 1C). Severe osteopenia leads to spine scoliosis and compression fracture of the 8th thoracic spine (Fig 1B). The curvatures of legs revealed genu valgum with intermalleolar distance (IMD) of 5.0cm (Fig 1D). There was no rachitic rosary observed.
